_why: Which prerendered pages build-cf.mjs copies into .open-next/assets so Cloudflare answers them WITHOUT starting the Worker. The OpenNext Worker imports its 45 MB server bundle on the first request of every cold isolate (measured ~0.9 s CPU; the free plan allows 10 ms), so any request that reaches the Worker can fail with error 1102; a file in assets costs ~3 ms and no Worker invocation. scripts/static-pages-to-assets.mjs DISCOVERS the routes from .next/prerender-manifest.json: every fully static route (initialRevalidateSeconds === false) is copied unless it is excluded below, plus ISR routes under isrStaticPrefixes. Trade-offs of bypassing the Worker (see docs/runbooks/cloudflare-web-deploy.md): middleware.ts does not run (no portal 307 for signed-out visitors, no ?lang= handling; the poojly_language cookie is written by an inline script in app/layout.tsx on locale landings, the `/` language redirect is HomeLocaleRedirect, and Content-Language comes from public/_headers), the asset layer ignores query strings and request headers, and a client-side soft navigation to these paths falls back to a full page load (the RSC request is answered with HTML).

mustBeStatic._why: Build FAILS if any of these routes is missing from the prerender output or is not fully static. portalPrefixes must list every PORTAL_PREFIXES entry of middleware.ts (a test pins that): every page route under them must be fully static, or be listed in workerServed with its reason.

workerServed._why: Page routes under portalPrefixes that legitimately stay on the Worker (dynamic [param] segments or server-rendered). Anything else under a portal prefix that stops being static fails the build.
workerServed./admin/users/[id]: dynamic segment, no generateStaticParams; /admin/users/view is the static twin
workerServed./priest/bookings/[id]: dynamic segment; /priest/bookings/view is the static twin

exclude._why: Static routes that MUST reach the Worker. Everything else static is copied.

prefixes./static-shell/: internal rewrite targets of middleware (/pujas, /store); never a public URL

isrStaticPrefixes._why: Sections that are ISR only because of `export const revalidate` but render committed in-repo data (no fetch, no cookies, no dates; verified by __tests__/cf-static-assets.test.ts). The Workers incremental cache is read-only, so these never refresh between deploys anyway; copying them only removes the cold-Worker hit. Live-data sections (temples, pujas, panchang, blog, store, wellness, astrology, city, yatra-packages, deity, festival, calendar, help, content ISR) are deliberately NOT here.

isrStaticRoutes._why: Exact routes copied to assets although Next marks them ISR (a fetch inside the page tree carries a revalidate window). The page itself is clock- and cookie-free: everything dated or visitor-specific on it resolves in the browser. '/' also replaces middleware's language redirect with HomeLocaleRedirect. 2026-10-30: the committed-data tool pages under /astrology (their date inputs and 'today' defaults live inside ClientOnly or client components, nothing dated is rendered on the server), /nri/ca, /matchmaking, /sankalp and /discover. /astrology itself (live availability), /astrology/horoscope/<rashi> (today's date) and /astrology/[id] stay on the Worker.

isrBuildDataPrefixes._why: Sections whose pages read the API (or committed data) once at build time and contain nothing that depends on the clock, a cookie or a query string (checked 2026-10-29: no new Date()/Date.now()/cookies()/headers()/searchParams in the server tree of these sections; __tests__/cf-static-assets.test.ts re-checks it). The Workers incremental cache is read-only, so these never refreshed between deploys anyway; their content changes with a redeploy. Only routes that were actually prerendered are copied; unknown slugs (dynamicParams) still reach the Worker. NOT here on purpose: /panchang (city pages and index: dated), /today (dated), /astrology and /wellness/classes|instructors (sessions and availability), /pujas and /store (query-aware), /content (searchParams), /darshan/[id]/replay. 2026-10-30: /panchang/yoga and /panchang/karana (committed tables, no date) and /help/articles/* (Content-Language per path locale is now set by public/_headers rules, same as the locale landings; middleware.ts does not run for them). /panchang/<city> stays on the Worker (today's date). Also /festival and /calendar (2026-10-30): 'next festival', 'In N days', 'Today' and the past-dimming are applied in the browser (app/festival/FestivalLive.tsx, app/calendar/CalendarTodayMarkers.tsx); the server HTML carries no date logic.

mustBeCopied._why: Build FAILS if one of these is not copied to assets (a page that stopped being prerendered would silently go back to the Worker).

isrBuildDataPatterns._why: Single-segment pages of a section whose index page reads searchParams: only the pages matching `match` are copied, and __tests__/cf-static-assets.test.ts applies the build-time-data check to `dir` only. /content/<slug> is the committed-library reader; /content (the filtered index) stays on the Worker. /pujas/<slug> (the puja detail pages generateStaticParams prerenders from the API at build) and /pujas/<slug>/temples and /pujas/home-puja/<slug> join them (2026-10-30): the server tree of each reads no cookie, header, query or clock; price and temple data are read at build time, like /deity, /temples and /city (content changes with a redeploy). /pujas itself (query-aware index) and /pujas/<slug>/book (a redirect that forwards ?temple=, which the asset layer cannot match on) stay on the Worker.
